title: Eight-round AES-192 single-key MITM key recovery, low-data tradeoff

target.description: Eight-round AES-192 under the author's zero-based round numbering, rounds 0 through 7, with the real AES-192 key schedule and the reduced cipher's final MixColumns omitted.

setting.key_relation: One unknown secret AES key; the attacker does not select related keys or obtain related-key oracles.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: chosen-plaintext structures under one secret key
assumptions: Chosen-plaintext structures and the source's truncated-differential analysis.
The real AES-192 key-schedule relations in Propositions 3 and 4 are used to enumerate candidate subkey bytes.
The low-data variant checks multiple differentials with larger precomputed multiset tables, as in the end of Section 4.1.
Low-memory output-active byte restricted to1,6,11,12; low-data variant tests y5with one extra table parameter.

time.note: Author-reported AES-encryption-equivalent time from Table 1 and Section 4.1; the optimized tradeoff's separate preprocessing budget is not extracted.

data.note: Low-data variant at the end of Section 4.1, using multiple differentials in parallel on the same plaintext structures.

memory.note: Storage for the enlarged precomputed tables; the source explicitly measures this memory in 128-bit AES blocks.

preprocessing.note: Precomputed tables are required, but a separate preprocessing budget for the low-data variant is not extracted; missing does not mean zero.

success.description: The source analyzes an expected suitable pair or table hit but does not supply a numerical success probability for this Table 1 tradeoff.

review.scope: The defining section and table give expected right-pair/table-hit counts, conditional filtering and completion, but no numerical complete-key recovery probability at this retained parameter choice.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.4-5, Section 2.1, conventions and units; p.8, Table 1, AES-192 8-round row with data 2^107; pp.13-15, Section 4.1, especially Propositions 3-4 and the concluding data-memory tradeoff.
evidence.interpretation: The authors report time 2^172, data 2^107 chosen plaintexts and memory 2^96 AES blocks for the multiple-differential variant. The derivation uses the ordinary AES-192 key schedule, not a related-key oracle. This is an attack construction, not a security lower bound; unreported numerical success and separate preprocessing remain null.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.1–17 complete read; p.5native units; pp.10–13 seven-round costs and completion; pp.14–16 schedule-dependent extensions.
evidence.interpretation: Raw-first independent full inventory, original-PDF SHA recheck, bounded official version/successor checks. Existing quoted resource tuple and stableIDpreserved; no author code executed.

evidence.locator: PDF13–15 §4.1 and PDF5 single-key setting; two source differential layouts of the same8round extension.
evidence.interpretation: Source-supported semantic normalization of existing key-relation wording and designated target; no added oracle or key-control assumption.

evidence.locator: PDF8 Table1; PDF13–15 Section4.1, simple extension and 64 parallel differentials.
evidence.interpretation: Targeted success audit: expected counts and conditional correctness are retained without inventing an end-to-end probability or a Poisson independence assumption.

limitations: The attack, multiset tables and reported costs have not been independently executed or reproduced.
Unknown numerical success and separate preprocessing prevent automatic frontier comparison.
